raw_text:
Here’s a 12‑week, moderate‑intensity, heart‑rate–capped general fitness program suitable for a 58‑year‑old male six months post‑MI, cleared for moderate exercise. It emphasizes gradual progression, aerobic base, circulation-friendly resistance training, movement quality, and recovery. All strength work avoids Valsalva, uses controlled tempo, and submaximal loads; all conditioning stays below 70% age‑predicted HRmax (~115 bpm) or RPE 3–4/10. Include a 5–10 minute warm‑up and 5–10 minute cool‑down every session.

Global guidelines and guardrails
- Frequency: 4 days/week (2 full‑body strength + 2 low‑impact cardio/conditioning), plus optional light activity.
- Intensity caps: HR ≤115 bpm; RPE 3–4 for cardio, 4–5 for strength sets. Stop if chest pain, unusual shortness of breath, dizziness, palpitations, or undue fatigue. Keep at least 48 hours between strength days.
- Breathing: Exhale on exertion, inhale on return; no breath holding. Use talking test (should be able to speak in full sentences).
- Tempo: Controlled 2–3 seconds down, 1–2 seconds up; full, pain‑free ROM.
- Progression: Favor volume and density over load; increase only one variable at a time by small amounts.
- BP considerations: Seated or supported positions are fine; avoid prolonged overhead straining. Prefer machines/cables/dumbbells over heavy barbells initially.
- Warm‑up each session: 5–10 minutes easy cardio (HR ≤100 bpm), mobility for hips/shoulders/thoracic spine, and 1–2 light ramp‑up sets for first two lifts.
- Cool‑down: 5–10 minutes easy cardio, breathing drills (nasal or pursed‑lip), gentle stretching.

Phase overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Reintroduction and movement quality; build aerobic base at low‑moderate intensity; light full‑body strength.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Progressive volume; introduce short, HR‑capped intervals; modest strength progression.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Build density and stamina; gentle circuit elements; light power/mobility emphasis without spikes in HR.
- Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Consolidate; small increases in total work; prep for ongoing independent training.

Weekly structure (same pattern all 12 weeks, with progressions noted week‑by‑week)
- Day 1: Full‑Body Strength A + short cardio finisher (easy)
- Day 2: Steady‑State Cardio (low impact) + mobility
- Day 3: Full‑Body Strength B + short cardio finisher (easy)
- Day 4: Cardio Intervals (HR‑capped) or varied cardio + mobility
- Optional: 1–2 light walks (20–30 min) on off‑days at conversational pace

Exercise selection notes
- Choose machine or dumbbell variations that allow stable posture and easy load control.
- Substitute as needed for joint comfort; aim for symmetrical push/pull/hinge/squat, single‑leg support, core.

Phase 1: Weeks 1–3 — Foundation and Familiarization
Goal: Establish tolerance to regular training, reinforce breathing, stay well below HR cap while building consistency.

Week 1
- Day 1 Strength A
  - Leg Press (or Box Squat to high box): 2–3 sets x 10–12 reps, RPE 4, 90 sec rest
  - Seated Chest Press (machine): 2 x 10–12, RPE 4, 90 sec
  - Lat Pulldown (neutral grip): 2 x 10–12, RPE 4, 90 sec
  - Seated Cable Row: 2 x 10–12, RPE 4, 90 sec
  - DB RDL (light, to mid‑shin, soft knees): 2 x 10, RPE 4, 90 sec
  - Standing Cable Pallof Press: 2 x 8–10/side, 60 sec
  - Finisher: 5–8 minutes easy bike or treadmill walk, HR ≤105 bpm
- Day 2 Cardio
  - 20–25 minutes recumbent bike or treadmill incline 1–2%, HR 100–110 bpm (≤115), RPE 3
  - Mobility: 10 minutes hips, thoracic rotation, calf/hamstring stretches
- Day 3 Strength B
  - Goblet Squat to box (or Sit‑to‑Stand): 2 x 8–10, RPE 4
  - Assisted Split Squat (hands on support) or Step‑Up low box: 2 x 8/leg, RPE 4
  - One‑Arm DB Bench (flat) or Machine Chest Press: 2 x 8–10/arm, RPE 4
  - Chest‑Supported DB Row: 2 x 10–12, RPE 4
  - Cable Face Pull: 2 x 12–15, RPE 4
  - Dead Bug (feet on bench) or Heel Slides: 2 x 6–8/side, slow
  - Finisher: 5–8 minutes easy elliptical or walk, HR ≤105 bpm
- Day 4 Cardio Variability
  - 20 minutes elliptical or bike, HR 100–110 bpm; finish with 5 minutes breathing and stretches

Week 2
- Same structure; add 1 set to first two lifts each strength day (now 3 sets for primary pushes/pulls or legs).
- Cardio: 22–28 minutes, same HR cap; add 1–2 minutes total time or a slight incline.

Week 3
- Strength: Keep sets; add 1–2 reps per set where RPE ≤4; maintain breathing.
- Cardio: 25–30 minutes steady state; HR 105–112 bpm, not exceeding 115.

Phase 2: Weeks 4–6 — Progressive Volume and HR‑Capped Intervals
Goal: Slowly increase total work; introduce gentle intervals without exceeding HR cap.

Week 4
- Day 1 Strength A
  - Leg Press: 3 x 10–12, RPE 4–5
  - Seated Chest Press: 3 x 10–12, RPE 4–5
  - Lat Pulldown: 3 x 10–12, RPE 4–5
  - DB RDL: 3 x 10, RPE 4–5
  - Pallof Press: 2–3 x 10/side
  - Finisher: 8–10 minutes easy bike, HR ≤110
- Day 2 Cardio Intervals (intro)
  - 5 min easy warm‑up
  - 6–8 x 1 minute “moderate” efforts (HR 108–112) with 2 minutes easy between (HR ≤100)
  - 5 min cool‑down. Total 25–30 minutes. Never exceed 115 bpm.
- Day 3 Strength B
  - Goblet Box Squat: 3 x 8–10
  - Assisted Split Squat or Step‑Up: 3 x 8/leg
  - Chest‑Supported Row: 3 x 10–12
  - Cable Chest Fly or Pec Deck (light): 2–3 x 12
  - Cable Face Pull: 2–3 x 12–15
  - Dead Bug or Side Plank (knees): 2–3 x 20–30 sec/side
  - Finisher: 8–10 minutes easy walk
- Day 4 Steady Cardio
  - 28–32 minutes, HR 105–112, conversational pace

Week 5
- Strength: Add a set to lower‑body primary (now 4 sets) if RPE ≤5; otherwise add 1–2 reps.
- Intervals: 8–10 x 1 minute moderate (HR 110–113) with 90–120 sec easy; same total time.
- Steady cardio: 30–34 minutes, HR ≤112.

Week 6
- Strength: Keep sets; increase load 2–5% if all reps clean at RPE ≤5; otherwise hold.
- Intervals: Progress some to 75 sec work / 90–120 sec easy, maintaining HR ≤115.
- Optional technique: Light sled push/pull 2 x 20–30 m at walking pace on Strength B, if available, HR‑capped.

Phase 3: Weeks 7–9 — Density and Stamina
Goal: Maintain intensity cap while gently increasing density (more work in similar time) and adding circuit flow.

Week 7
- Day 1 Strength A (pairings to reduce rest without HR spike)
  - Pair 1: Leg Press 3 x 10–12 (RPE 5) with Seated Row 3 x 10–12; 60–75 sec between moves; monitor HR
  - Pair 2: Machine Chest Press 3 x 10–12 with Hamstring Curl 3 x 10–12
  - Core: Pallof Press 2–3 x 10/side; Breathing drill 2 min
  - Finisher: 6–8 min easy cardio
- Day 2 Cardio Intervals
  - 5 min warm‑up
  - 6 x 2 minutes moderate (HR 110–114) + 2 minutes easy (≤100)
  - 5 min cool‑down (total ~29–33 min)
- Day 3 Strength B (circuit of 4, repeat 2–3 rounds; rest 60–75 sec between stations as needed; keep HR ≤115)
  - Goblet Box Squat 8–10
  - Chest‑Supported Row 10–12
  - DB Incline Press or Machine Press 8–10
  - Cable Wood Chop 8–10/side
  - Accessory: Face Pull 2 x 12–15
- Day 4 Steady Cardio
  - 30–36 minutes, HR 105–112; optional change of modality (swim easy, elliptical, rower gentle)

Week 8
- Strength: Add one round (now 3 rounds) on Day 3 if HR remains ≤115; or add 1–2 reps per station.
- Intervals: 7 x 2 minutes moderate + 2 minutes easy, same caps.
- Steady cardio: +2–3 minutes time or very slight incline/resistance.

Week 9
- Strength: Small load bump (2–5%) on major patterns if RPE ≤5 and HR stable; keep reps.
- Intervals: 5 x 3 minutes moderate (HR 110–114) + 2 minutes easy; total ~30–32 minutes.
- Add balance work: Single‑leg stance with support 2 x 20–30 sec/leg on strength days.

Phase 4: Weeks 10–12 — Consolidation and Independence
Goal: Solidify habits, modest increases in total weekly work, prepare a maintainable template.

Week 10
- Day 1 Strength A (straight sets; slightly higher total volume)
  - Leg Press 4 x 10–12
  - Seated Row 3 x 10–12
  - Machine Chest Press 3 x 10–12
  - Hamstring Curl 3 x 10–12
  - Pallof Press 2–3 x 10/side
- Day 2 Cardio Intervals
  - 10 x 90 sec moderate (HR 110–114) + 90 sec easy
- Day 3 Strength B
  - Goblet Squat 3 x 10
  - Step‑Up (medium box) 3 x 8/leg
  - DB Incline or Machine Press 3 x 10
  - Chest‑Supported Row 3 x 10–12
  - Face Pull 2–3 x 12–15
  - Side Plank (knees or feet) 2 x 20–30 sec/side
- Day 4 Steady Cardio
  - 32–38 minutes, HR 105–112

Week 11
- Strength: Add 1 set to upper push or pull where tolerated (total weekly sets +2–3).
- Intervals: 6 x 3 minutes moderate + 2 minutes easy; HR ≤115.
- Steady cardio: Maintain duration, aim for slightly quicker comfortable cadence without HR spike.

Week 12
- Strength: Keep sets; focus on perfect technique and breathing; optional circuit on Day 3 to practice flow:
  - Circuit x 3 rounds: Box Squat 10, Seated Row 10–12, Machine Press 10, Cable Wood Chop 10/side, Farmer Carry light 30–40 m (walk and breathe)
- Intervals: 8 x 2 minutes moderate + 2 minutes easy; finish feeling fresh.
- Steady cardio: 34–40 minutes at HR 105–112.

Recovery, monitoring, and lifestyle
- Daily: 10–15 minute walks as desired at easy pace; gentle mobility on off‑days.
- Rate of perceived exertion: Strength sets RPE 4–5 (stop with 3–5 reps in reserve); cardio RPE 3–4.
- Hydration: ~2–3 L/day unless medically restricted. Avoid heavy meals right before training; allow 1–2 hours post‑meal.
- Sleep: Aim 7–8 hours/night; consistent schedule.
- Warning signs to stop and refer: Chest discomfort/pressure, unusual shortness of breath, nausea, lightheadedness, palpitations, radiating pain, or BP symptoms. If these occur, cease exercise, follow medical plan, and seek care.

Basic nutrition guidance (general fitness, heart‑healthy; align with any cardiologist/dietitian advice)
- Emphasize vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains, nuts/seeds; lean proteins (fish 2x/week, poultry, tofu/tempeh, low‑fat dairy).
- Prefer unsaturated fats (olive oil, avocado); limit saturated fat, trans fats, excessive sodium; minimize ultra‑processed foods.
- Protein target: ~1.0–1.2 g/kg/day unless contraindicated; distribute across meals for recovery.
- Carbohydrates: Base around training windows; choose high‑fiber sources; stay hydrated.
- Caffeine/alcohol per medical guidance.

Testing and progression notes
- No max lifts. Use submax tests such as:
  - Talk test and RPE each session.
  - Optional 6‑minute walk distance at Week 1 and Week 12 to gauge improvement, keeping HR ≤115.
- Adjust loads weekly so last 2–3 reps feel challenging but never force breath holding or technique breakdown.
- If HR approaches 115 during sets, extend rests, reduce load, or switch to more supported machine variations.

Contingencies and substitutions
- Joint discomfort: swap goblet squats for leg press; swap RDLs for hamstring curl; swap bench for machine press.
- Equipment: If limited, use cable columns, bodyweight, and light dumbbells; keep same movement patterns.
- Illness or poor recovery week: Reduce volume by 30–50%, skip intervals in favor of steady easy cardio, and resume next week.

By Week 12 he should tolerate 4 sessions/week comfortably, perform 8–12 rep strength sets with steady breathing, complete 30–40 minutes of HR‑capped cardio, and be ready to continue with a similar structure or modest progressions, always respecting the 70% HRmax cap and clinical guidance.
